name: Midlothian
seo_title: Midlothian, TX Christmas Events for Kids 2026: 5 Events
seo_description: Kids' Christmas in Midlothian, TX: the City Hall tree lighting, Christmas Glow Light-Up Parade, Merry Movie Night, Santa photos and carriage rides.
lede: The story of Christmas in Midlothian begins with a Scottish train engineer who suggested the town's name in the early 1880s, just before the Gulf, Colorado and Santa Fe Railway reached it in 1883. Today the city lights its Christmas tree on the steps of City Hall and sends the Christmas Glow Light-Up Parade through downtown.
sections: The tree lighting and the Christmas Glow Light-Up Parade

Midlothian's season opens at City Hall, 215 N 8th Street, with the Annual Christmas Tree Lighting Ceremony on Tuesday, December 1, 2026, at 6 pm. The city's calendar sets the rain date for Wednesday, December 2, at 6 pm, lists the event as free and runs a tree lighter random drawing contest. Four days later, on Saturday, December 5, the Christmas Glow Light-Up Parade runs from 6 to 8 pm in downtown Midlothian, starting at the 8th Street bridge. On Friday, December 11, Merry Movie Night shows Home Alone on the lawn at Midlothian Community Park from 6:30 to 9 pm, free, and families are asked to bring blankets and chairs.
Merry and Bright: Santa photos and carriage rides

The City of Midlothian runs Merry and Bright at City Hall with free photos with Santa on Saturday, December 12, 2026, from 1 to 4 pm. On Friday and Saturday, December 18 and 19, free horse drawn carriage rides circle the downtown square from 5 to 7 pm, leaving from the north side of City Hall under the Midlothian mural. Also in December, Back Porch Theatre stages Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer JR. at the Midlothian Civic Center, 224 S 11th Street, on December 16, 17 and 18 at 7 pm, with tickets at $15 for adults and $10 for children plus fees.
A town named by a train engineer

The Handbook of Texas traces Midlothian to 1848, when the Hawkins and Newton families received land titles under the Peters colony and the place was known as Hawkins' Springs. A post office called Barker opened in 1877. In 1882 or 1883 the name changed to Midlothian, suggested by a Scottish train engineer after a place in his home country, and the Gulf, Colorado and Santa Fe tracks arrived in 1883. The town incorporated in April 1888 and later became known as the Cement Capitol of Texas for its Portland cement industry. For train rides and displays, the Interurban Railway Museum in Plano and the Museum of the American Railroad in Frisco have Rally pages.

faq: How did Midlothian get its name?

The Handbook of Texas says a post office called Barker opened in 1877. In 1882 or 1883 the name changed to Midlothian, suggested by a Scottish train engineer after a place in his home country. The Gulf, Colorado and Santa Fe tracks arrived in 1883, just after the new name took hold.

The Handbook of Texas traces Midlothian to 1848, when the Hawkins and Newton families received land titles under the Peters colony and the place was known as Hawkins' Springs. The town incorporated in April 1888 and later became known as the Cement Capitol of Texas for its Portland cement industry.
What happens at Christmas for kids in Midlothian?

The Christmas Tree Lighting Ceremony is Tuesday, December 1, 2026, at 6 pm on the steps of City Hall, with a rain date of December 2. The Christmas Glow Light-Up Parade follows on December 5 from 6 to 8 pm downtown. Merry Movie Night shows Home Alone on December 11, free.
Can kids see Santa for free in Midlothian?

Yes. The City of Midlothian runs Merry and Bright at City Hall, 215 N 8th Street, with free photos with Santa on Saturday, December 12, 2026, from 1 to 4 pm. Free horse drawn carriage rides circle the downtown square on December 18 and 19 from 5 to 7 pm.
Who organizes Christmas events in Midlothian?

The City of Midlothian runs the tree lighting, the Christmas Glow Light-Up Parade, Merry Movie Night and Merry and Bright, and lists them on its calendar and news pages. Back Porch Theatre stages Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer JR. at the Midlothian Civic Center on December 16, 17 and 18 at 7 pm.
